name: Ammizabad
overview: Ammizabad is a male figure identified as the son of Benaiah. He is noted for his leadership role, specifically being placed over the third division, indicating a position of authority or responsibility. His tribal affiliation is not specified in the biblical record provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Ammizabad means '[my] people have given a gift,' reflecting a Hebrew origin and possibly indicating a sense of divine or communal blessing. This is the sole name recorded for him in Scripture, without additional titles.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ammizabad as the son of Benaiah. No further family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Ammizabad's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his administrative role, overseeing the third division as part of a structured leadership system. His position underlines the organized governance present in Israel during the period referenced. Being the son of Benaiah, a notable figure, also situates Ammizabad within a lineage of trusted leaders.
